topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening welcome, introduces the scope of the lecture series, and outlines the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cellular and tissue-level foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the fundamental concepts of cancer development through genetic alterations, failure of tissue differentiation architecture, and the experimental models used to study cellular transformation.

topics.label: Characteristics, histology, and progression of benign versus malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the defining features of benign and malignant tumors, detailing local invasion, metastatic dissemination, histological identification, and stepwise neoplastic progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standardized naming rules and notable exceptions for classifying benign and malignant neoplasms based on their cell and tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the mechanical, functional, and systemic processes through which primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across human populations and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare epidemiological patterns of tumor incidence and mortality in humans with tumor occurrences across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Rationale, histopathology, and practice of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the clinical rationale for early detection and evaluate the screening techniques, histopathological criteria, and limitations across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with closing remarks, a reminder of the learning outcomes, and housekeeping instructions for the upcoming practicals.
